html:
Daniel O'Connell was an Irish lawyer and politician, called the Liberator, who won Catholic emancipation in 1829.

Under the laws left from the Protestant Ascendancy, Catholics could not sit in parliament. In 1823 O'Connell founded the Catholic Association, paid for by a penny a month from poor members, which made millions of peasants into a political force. In 1828 he was elected to parliament for County Clare, though as a Catholic he could not take his seat. Fearing revolt, the government gave way.

He then campaigned to repeal the Act of Union with huge open-air meetings, but always without violence, and called off a rally in 1843 when the army was sent. He died in 1847, during the Great Famine. His methods inspired later mass movements. See Ireland.
sum: Daniel O'Connell was an Irish lawyer and politician, called the Liberator, who won Catholic emancipation in 1829.
